label: GB-ico-ai-data-protection-guidance How do we ensure individual rights in our AI systems?

obligations.text: When procuring an AI service, you must choose one which allows individual rights to be protected and enabled, in order to meet your obligations as a controller.
If you are operating as a controller, your contract with the processor must stipulate that the processor assist you in responding to rights requests.

Right to be informed
You must inform individuals if their personal data is going to be used to train an AI system, to ensure that processing is fair and transparent.

Under Articles 13 (2)(f) and 14 (2)(g), you must tell people whose data you are processing that you are doing so for automated decision-making and give them “meaningful information about the logic involved, as well as the significance and the envisaged consequences” of the processing for them.
Under Article 15 (2)(h) you must also tell them about this if they submit a subject access request.
Human intervention should involve a review of the decision, which must be carried out by someone with the appropriate authority and capability to change that decision.
Note that if you are using automated decision making, as well as implementing suitable safeguards, you must also have a suitable lawful basis.

They should have actual ‘meaningful’ influence on the decision, including the ‘authority and competence’ to go against the recommendation; and
reviewers must ‘weigh-up’ and ‘interpret’ the recommendation, consider all available input data, and also take into account other additional factors.
You must also ensure clear lines of accountability and effective risk management policies are in place from the outset.
You must think about what features you expect the AI system to consider and which additional factors the human reviewers should take into account before finalising their decision.
Those in charge of designing the front-end interface of an AI system must understand the needs, thought processes, and behaviours of human reviewers and allow them to effectively intervene.
